pesticide.seedling: Apply mancozeb at HALF DOSE (1g/L). Spray early morning only. Reapply after rain. Avoid direct sun exposure on treated seedlings.
pesticide.mature: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at full label rate. Rotate fungicides every 2 applications to prevent resistance. Spray every 7-10 days until lesions stop expanding.

organic.seedling: Dilute neem oil to 2.5 ml/L (half strength). Apply weekly in evening. Remove badly affected seedlings to prevent nursery-wide spread.
organic.mature: Neem oil 5 ml/L with liquid soap as surfactant. Compost tea foliar spray bi-weekly. Bacillus subtilis biological control as preventive.

pruning.seedling: Gently remove only severely spotted cotyledons. Do not over-prune young plants — they need leaf area to establish. Disinfect tools between plants.
pruning.mature: Remove all affected lower leaves. Cut 2 cm below visible lesion margin. Bag and dispose — never compost infected material. Disinfect shears between cuts with 10% bleach.

watering.seedling: Water at soil level using drip irrigation. Keep soil moist but not waterlogged. Avoid splashing soil onto leaves. Morning watering preferred.
watering.mature: Morning watering only at soil level. Improve air circulation with wider spacing. Add straw mulch 3-4 inches to reduce soil splash. Avoid overhead irrigation completely.

pesticide.seedling: Apply metalaxyl at HALF DOSE immediately. Isolate affected seedlings. Preventive copper spray on healthy neighbours at 1g/L.
pesticide.mature: Apply metalaxyl-M + mancozeb at full rate immediately. Spray every 5-7 days during wet weather. Switch to cymoxanil after 2 applications to prevent resistance.

organic.seedling: Copper hydroxide at half strength (1g/L). Remove and destroy all infected seedlings. Apply Trichoderma-based biocontrol to remaining plants.
organic.mature: Copper hydroxide 2g/L — spray entire canopy including undersides. Bordeaux mixture (1:1:10) as alternative. Destroy all infected plant material immediately.

pruning.seedling: Remove entire infected seedlings — do not prune, destroy whole plant. Bag in sealed plastic before moving through nursery.
pruning.mature: Remove all infected branches and 15 cm of healthy tissue beyond visible symptoms. Double-bag in sealed plastic. Burn or dispose in landfill — NEVER compost.

watering.seedling: Reduce watering immediately. No overhead watering under any circumstances. Improve ventilation in nursery. Increase plant spacing.
watering.mature: Stop all overhead irrigation. Water only at soil level, early morning. Maximize air flow — remove lower canopy. Improve drainage. Consider raised beds for future plantings.

pesticide.seedling: Apply azoxystrobin at HALF DOSE at V6 stage if lesions appear early. Monitor closely for 7 days before retreating.
pesticide.mature: Apply propiconazole or azoxystrobin at full rate at tasseling. Spray upper leaves thoroughly. Single application usually sufficient unless wet weather persists.

organic.seedling: Neem oil 3 ml/L foliar spray. Ensure adequate nitrogen nutrition to boost plant resistance. Avoid planting in fields with corn residue.
organic.mature: Bacillus subtilis foliar spray. Remove lower infected leaves if accessible. Maintain balanced fertility — excess nitrogen increases susceptibility.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected lower leaves by hand. Avoid mechanical damage to stalks. Dispose of removed leaves away from field.
pruning.mature: Remove severely infected lower leaves if disease is concentrated there. Focus on protecting ear leaf and above. Destroy crop residue after harvest.

watering.seedling: Maintain consistent soil moisture. Avoid water stress which increases susceptibility. Morning irrigation preferred.
watering.mature: Continue regular irrigation schedule. Avoid overhead irrigation if possible. Ensure good field drainage. Avoid working in wet fields to reduce spore spread.

pesticide.seedling: Apply captan at half rate during first leaf emergence. Begin spray program at green tip stage. Reapply every 7 days during wet spring weather.
pesticide.mature: Apply myclobutanil or captan at full rate. Begin at green tip, continue through petal fall. Spray every 7-10 days. Rotate fungicide classes each season.

organic.seedling: Sulfur spray at 3g/L beginning at green tip. Apply before rain events. Avoid sulfur in temperatures above 30°C to prevent leaf burn.
organic.mature: Sulfur or lime-sulfur spray pre-bloom. Neem oil post-bloom. Remove fallen leaves in autumn to reduce overwintering inoculum. Apply compost to stimulate leaf decomposition.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected leaves promptly. Thin young trees to improve air circulation. Disinfect pruning tools.
pruning.mature: Open canopy pruning to improve airflow and light penetration. Remove water sprouts and crossing branches. Collect and destroy all fallen infected leaves and fruit.

watering.seedling: Water at base only. Avoid wetting foliage. Keep nursery area well-drained.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation only — avoid sprinklers. Morning watering to allow foliage drying. Improve soil drainage around root zone.

pesticide.seedling: Apply captan at half rate if cankers appear on young wood. Focus on wound protection after any pruning.
pesticide.mature: Apply captan or thiophanate-methyl during early season. Target sprays from pink through second cover. Protect pruning wounds with fungicide paste.

organic.seedling: Copper spray at half strength after pruning. Seal pruning cuts with organic wound paste. Maintain plant vigor with balanced nutrition.
organic.mature: Copper hydroxide spray at petal fall. Remove mummified fruit and dead wood — primary inoculum sources. Apply Trichoderma-based biocontrol to pruning wounds.

pruning.seedling: Remove any cankered wood 15 cm below visible symptoms. Fire-sterilize pruning tools between cuts.
pruning.mature: Remove all dead wood, cankers, and mummified fruit. Prune at least 15 cm below canker margin. Burn pruned material — do not leave in orchard. Prune during dry weather.

watering.seedling: Moderate watering. Avoid drought stress which predisposes to infection. Good drainage essential.
watering.mature: Maintain consistent moisture to reduce stress. Avoid drought periods followed by heavy watering. Mulch to stabilize soil moisture.

pesticide.seedling: Apply myclobutanil at half rate at pink bud stage. Continue every 7 days through petal fall.
pesticide.mature: Apply myclobutanil or triadimefon from pink bud through 2nd cover spray. Most critical period is bloom through 3 weeks post-petal fall.

organic.seedling: Sulfur spray at half rate from pink bud. Remove nearby juniper/cedar trees if possible — they are alternate hosts.
organic.mature: Sulfur or neem oil from pink bud stage. Remove galls from juniper/cedar within 1 mile radius if feasible. Plant resistant apple varieties.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected leaves. Keep nursery away from juniper/cedar trees.
pruning.mature: Remove heavily infected leaves and fruit. Cut out galls from nearby junipers in late winter before they produce spores.

watering.seedling: Avoid overhead watering. Keep foliage dry.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation only. Maximize air circulation. Avoid wetting foliage during the spring infection period.

pesticide.seedling: Apply mancozeb at half rate starting at 6-inch shoot growth. Continue every 7 days during wet weather.
pesticide.mature: Apply myclobutanil or mancozeb from immediate pre-bloom through 4-5 weeks post-bloom. This is the critical infection window. Spray every 7-10 days.

organic.seedling: Copper spray at half rate. Remove all mummified berries. Maintain open canopy.
organic.mature: Copper hydroxide pre-bloom, sulfur post-bloom. Remove ALL mummified berries — primary inoculum source. Compost tea as preventive spray.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected shoots and tendrils. Train vines for good air flow.
pruning.mature: Remove mummified berries and infected clusters immediately. Open canopy for maximum airflow and sunlight. Remove infected tendrils. Post-harvest, remove all leftover fruit.

watering.seedling: Drip irrigation only. Keep foliage dry. Ensure good drainage.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation only — never overhead. Water in morning. Manage canopy to maximize drying. Good weed management under vines.

pesticide.seedling: No effective chemical treatment for young vines. Focus on prevention — use clean planting material from reputable nurseries.
pesticide.mature: No curative fungicides available. Trichoderma-based trunk applications may slow progression. Sodium arsenite banned in most regions.

organic.seedling: Dip pruning wounds in Trichoderma suspension. Use only certified disease-free nursery stock.
organic.mature: Apply Trichoderma harzianum to pruning wounds immediately after cutting. Hot water treatment of dormant cuttings (50°C for 30 min) for new plantings.

pruning.seedling: Prune only in dry weather. Apply wound sealant to all cuts. Use clean, sterilized tools.
pruning.mature: Late pruning (delayed until after bud swell) reduces infection risk. Make clean cuts. Apply wound protectant paste immediately. Remove dead spurs and cordons.

watering.seedling: Avoid water stress. Consistent irrigation supports vine vigor against trunk diseases.
watering.mature: Maintain consistent soil moisture — stress exacerbates esca symptoms. Avoid drought-wet cycles. Mulch to stabilize moisture.

pesticide.seedling: Apply myclobutanil at HALF DOSE when white patches first appear. Avoid wetting foliage — this disease thrives in dry conditions with high humidity.
pesticide.mature: Apply sulfur or myclobutanil at full rate. Begin at first sign of white powdery growth. Spray every 7-14 days. Alternate chemistries to avoid resistance.

organic.seedling: Potassium bicarbonate 3g/L spray. Milk spray (1:9 ratio with water) is surprisingly effective. Apply in morning.
organic.mature: Neem oil 5 ml/L or potassium bicarbonate 5g/L. Sulfur dust on dry days. Baking soda 1 tbsp/gallon + liquid soap. Weekly applications.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected leaves promptly. Increase spacing for airflow.
pruning.mature: Open canopy pruning for air circulation. Remove infected shoots and leaves. Destroy — do not compost. Thin fruit clusters if overcrowded.

watering.seedling: Water at soil level. Good air circulation is more important than reducing humidity for this disease.
watering.mature: Overhead watering can actually help wash spores off leaves (unlike most diseases). But drip is still preferred. Improve air movement through canopy.

pesticide.seedling: Copper hydroxide at HALF DOSE + mancozeb. Apply preventively before symptoms appear in transplants. Weekly applications.
pesticide.mature: Copper hydroxide + mancozeb tank mix at full rate. Spray every 5-7 days during wet weather. Copper alone loses effectiveness — always combine.

organic.seedling: Copper spray at reduced rate. Avoid overhead watering. Remove severely infected seedlings from greenhouse.
organic.mature: Copper-based organic spray. Acibenzolar-S-methyl as systemic resistance inducer. Remove infected plants if disease is severe. Rotate fields.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected seedlings entirely. Do not prune — it spreads bacteria through wounds. Isolate healthy plants.
pruning.mature: Avoid pruning or handling wet plants — bacteria spread through wounds and splashing water. Remove severely infected plants entirely.

watering.seedling: Drip irrigation only. No overhead watering. Reduce leaf wetness duration. Water early morning.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation exclusively. Avoid working in fields when plants are wet. Reduce plant density for better air circulation.

pesticide.seedling: Copper hydroxide at half rate + mancozeb. Begin applications preventively in transplant greenhouse. Hot water seed treatment (50°C, 25 min).
pesticide.mature: Copper hydroxide + mancozeb at full rate every 5-7 days. Most effective when started preventively. Actigard (acibenzolar-S-methyl) as resistance inducer.

organic.seedling: Copper-based organic fungicide at reduced rate. Hot water seed treatment. Use disease-free transplants.
organic.mature: Copper spray + Bacillus subtilis biocontrol. Serenade (B. subtilis) biofungicide. Rotate out of solanaceous crops for 2 years.

pruning.seedling: Remove entire infected seedlings. Do not prune — bacterial spread through wounds.
pruning.mature: Remove severely infected lower leaves when dry. Avoid handling wet plants. Destroy removed material. Stake plants for better airflow.

watering.seedling: Bottom watering only. Keep foliage completely dry. Good greenhouse ventilation.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation only. No overhead irrigation. Water in morning. Staking and mulching reduce splash from soil.

pesticide.seedling: Apply chlorothalonil at half rate if growing in greenhouse. Increase ventilation immediately.
pesticide.mature: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at full rate. Most important in greenhouse/high tunnel production. Spray every 7-10 days.

organic.seedling: Improve ventilation — this is the most effective treatment. Neem oil 2.5 ml/L. Reduce humidity below 85%.
organic.mature: Increase ventilation and air circulation. Neem oil 5 ml/L. Sulfur spray. Reduce humidity — open vents, use fans. Remove lower leaves.

pruning.seedling: Thin seedlings to improve airflow. Remove any leaves with olive-green fuzzy growth on underside.
pruning.mature: Remove infected lower leaves. Open canopy for maximum airflow. Remove suckers. Bag and destroy infected material.

watering.seedling: Water at soil level only. Reduce humidity. Increase ventilation. Morning watering.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation only. Keep relative humidity below 85%. Use fans in greenhouses. Avoid creating microclimates of still, humid air.

pesticide.seedling: Apply mancozeb or chlorothalonil at half rate when first spots appear on lower leaves.
pesticide.mature: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or copper fungicide at full rate. Spray every 7-10 days. Begin when first spots appear on lower leaves.

organic.seedling: Copper spray at half rate. Remove affected lower leaves. Mulch to prevent soil splash.
organic.mature: Copper-based fungicide. Neem oil spray. Bacillus subtilis biocontrol. Aggressive lower leaf removal. 3-4 inch mulch layer.

pruning.seedling: Remove lowest leaves touching or near soil. These are first infected via rain splash.
pruning.mature: Remove all leaves below the first fruit cluster. Remove spotted leaves progressively. Bag and dispose. Stake or cage plants for elevation.

watering.seedling: Water at soil level. Mulch immediately around seedlings. Morning watering only.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation only. Heavy mulch layer (3-4 inches) to prevent soil splash — the primary infection route. Never overhead water.

pesticide.seedling: Apply abamectin at HALF DOSE. Target leaf undersides. Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill beneficial predators.
pesticide.mature: Apply abamectin or bifenazate at full rate. Thorough coverage of leaf undersides essential. Rotate miticides. Avoid pyrethroids — they worsen mite outbreaks.

organic.seedling: Strong water spray to dislodge mites. Neem oil 2.5 ml/L targeting undersides. Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
organic.mature: Neem oil 5 ml/L + insecticidal soap. Release predatory mites. Strong water blast to knock mites off. Repeat every 3-5 days until controlled.

pruning.seedling: Remove severely infested leaves. Check transplants before introducing to garden.
pruning.mature: Remove heavily infested lower leaves. Destroy — do not compost. Keep area weed-free as weeds harbor mites.

watering.seedling: Mites thrive in dry, dusty conditions. Maintain adequate moisture. Light misting can deter mites.
watering.mature: Overhead misting can suppress mites (exception to the usual rule). Maintain soil moisture — water stress dramatically increases mite populations. Reduce dust.

pesticide.seedling: Apply chlorothalonil at half rate when concentric ring spots appear. Begin preventive sprays in warm, humid conditions.
pesticide.mature: Apply chlorothalonil or boscalid + pyraclostrobin at full rate. Spray every 7-10 days. Most severe in warm, humid weather.

organic.seedling: Copper-based spray at half rate. Remove infected leaves. Improve air circulation.
organic.mature: Copper hydroxide spray. Neem oil. Remove all infected lower leaves. Increase spacing. Destroy crop debris after season.

pruning.seedling: Remove spotted leaves immediately. Thin for airflow.
pruning.mature: Aggressive lower leaf removal. Remove all spotted leaves. Open canopy. Stake or trellis plants for maximum air circulation.

watering.seedling: Water at base. Keep foliage dry. Morning watering only.
watering.mature: Drip irrigation exclusively. Mulch heavily. Avoid any overhead watering. Improve field drainage.

pesticide.seedling: Apply imidacloprid drench to control whitefly vectors. Use reflective mulch to repel whiteflies. Screen greenhouse openings.
pesticide.mature: No cure for virus — manage whitefly vectors with systemic insecticides (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam). Rotate insecticide classes.

organic.seedling: Yellow sticky traps for whiteflies. Neem oil spray. Reflective silver mulch deters whiteflies. Fine mesh insect netting.
organic.mature: Release Encarsia formosa parasitoid wasps. Neem oil for whitefly management. Yellow sticky traps. Remove infected plants promptly.

pruning.seedling: Remove and destroy ALL infected seedlings immediately — there is no cure. Bag before moving through nursery.
pruning.mature: Remove infected plants entirely and destroy. No amount of pruning will save an infected plant. Focus on protecting uninfected plants.

watering.seedling: Normal watering. Focus on vector (whitefly) management, not cultural practices.
watering.mature: Normal watering schedule. The virus is vector-transmitted (whiteflies), not water/splash-transmitted. Healthy plants resist virus better.

pesticide.seedling: No chemical cure. Disinfect all tools and hands with 10% bleach or milk solution. Remove infected plants.
pesticide.mature: No chemical cure available. Prevent mechanical spread: disinfect tools, wash hands, avoid handling wet plants. Remove and destroy infected plants.

organic.seedling: Dip hands in milk before handling plants (inactivates virus). Remove infected seedlings. Use certified virus-free seed.
organic.mature: Milk dip for hands and tools. Cross-protection with mild virus strains in some regions. Resistant varieties are the best solution.

pruning.seedling: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. NEVER prune — the virus spreads through sap on tools and hands.
pruning.mature: Remove entire infected plants. If you must work near infected plants, change gloves between each plant. Disinfect tools with 10% bleach between cuts.

watering.seedling: Normal watering. Virus is NOT water-transmitted — it spreads through direct contact and sap.
watering.mature: Normal watering. Focus on hygiene: hand washing, tool disinfection, avoiding tobacco products near plants (TMV persists in cured tobacco).

pesticide.seedling: Apply propiconazole at half rate if pustules appear on young tillers. Early-season rust can significantly reduce stand.
pesticide.mature: Apply propiconazole or tebuconazole at full rate when pustules appear on flag leaf or second leaf. Single well-timed spray usually sufficient.

organic.seedling: Sulfur spray at half rate. Plant resistant varieties — this is the most effective organic strategy. Remove volunteer wheat nearby.
organic.mature: Limited organic options for cereal rust. Sulfur spray. Focus on resistant varieties for future planting. Destroy crop residue after harvest.

pruning.seedling: Not applicable for wheat — focus on chemical/cultural controls.
pruning.mature: Not applicable. Destroy all crop residue and volunteer wheat after harvest to reduce overwintering inoculum.

watering.seedling: Maintain adequate moisture for healthy growth. Avoid drought stress which reduces natural resistance.
watering.mature: Continue normal irrigation. Avoid late-season excess moisture which extends the green leaf period and rust development.

pesticide.seedling: Apply copper hydroxide at half rate. Drain nursery fields. Use seed treatment with streptomycin sulfate before planting.
pesticide.mature: Limited chemical options. Copper-based bactericides provide partial control. Avoid excess nitrogen which increases susceptibility. No antibiotics registered in many regions.

organic.seedling: Copper-based spray. Use resistant varieties. Seed treatment with hot water (52°C for 30 min). Balanced nutrition.
organic.mature: Copper hydroxide spray. Reduce nitrogen rates by 25%. Drain and re-flood fields to reduce bacterial load. Resistant varieties are the primary control.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected seedlings from nursery. Clip leaf tips before transplanting to reduce infection sites.
pruning.mature: Remove severely infected tillers if feasible. Avoid unnecessary field traffic when leaves are wet. Remove ratoon crops promptly after harvest.

watering.seedling: Intermittent irrigation in nursery — avoid continuous flooding. Drain for 2-3 days if disease appears.
watering.mature: Drain fields for 3-5 days at mid-tillering if disease is severe. Reduce water depth. Intermittent irrigation reduces bacterial spread. Avoid deep flooding.

pesticide.seedling: No treatment needed. Continue routine preventive spray schedule if in disease-prone region. Monitor weekly for early symptoms.
pesticide.mature: No treatment needed. Maintain standard IPM preventive spray program. Scout weekly for any emerging issues.

organic.seedling: Routine compost tea foliar spray for general plant health. Maintain balanced organic nutrition. Continue monitoring.
organic.mature: Continue routine organic maintenance: compost tea, beneficial insect habitat, crop rotation planning. This leaf is healthy — celebrate good management.

pruning.seedling: Standard nursery maintenance only. No disease-related pruning needed.
pruning.mature: Standard seasonal pruning for shape and airflow. No disease-related pruning needed. Continue good hygiene practices.

watering.seedling: Maintain current watering schedule — plant is thriving. Consistent moisture promotes healthy growth.
watering.mature: Maintain current irrigation program. Healthy leaf tissue indicates good cultural practices. Continue monitoring.

pesticide.seedling: Monitor — rarely severe enough to warrant treatment in seedlings. Apply mancozeb at half rate only if pustules are dense.
pesticide.mature: Apply azoxystrobin + propiconazole at full rate if pustules reach mid-canopy before tasseling. Usually a single application is sufficient.

organic.seedling: Sulfur spray at half rate. Plant resistant hybrids. Ensure adequate nutrition.
organic.mature: Sulfur spray. Focus on resistant varieties for future seasons. Adequate potassium reduces severity. Destroy crop residue.

pruning.seedling: Remove lower infected leaves if accessible. Monitor progression.
pruning.mature: Not practical in corn. Focus on resistant hybrids and chemical control if severe. Destroy crop residue after harvest.

watering.seedling: Normal irrigation. Rust is airborne — not water-transmitted.
watering.mature: Normal irrigation schedule. Rust severity is primarily driven by weather (cool, humid nights with moderate days) rather than irrigation practices.

pesticide.seedling: Rarely affects seedlings. If spots appear, apply azoxystrobin at half rate. Rotate out of continuous corn.
pesticide.mature: Apply pyraclostrobin + metconazole between VT and R2 (tasseling to blister). Most effective as preventive before severe infection.

organic.seedling: Rotate away from corn-on-corn. Tillage to bury infected residue. Resistant hybrids.
organic.mature: Crop rotation is the most effective organic control. Tillage to bury residue. Avoid corn-on-corn. Resistant hybrids.

pruning.seedling: Remove infected lower leaves. Improve field drainage.
pruning.mature: Not practical in corn. Focus on rotation and resistant hybrids. Destroy crop residue thoroughly.

watering.seedling: Avoid overhead irrigation. Good drainage essential.
watering.mature: Avoid overhead irrigation if possible. Disease favors prolonged leaf wetness and high humidity. Improve field air circulation.
